summary: Documented M3-S04 (Case assignment rules and auto-response rules) after it reached `tested`. Re-rendered PLAN.md/CLARIFICATIONS.md from plan.json; appended 7 decisions.md entries covering the operator's pre-gate senderEmail resolution (D-M3S04-01), the deliberately-omitted Account-support-tier criterion and its title/test mismatch (D-M3S04-02), F-28's org-wide-address deploy prerequisite (D-M3S04-03), the replyToEmail/senderEmail threading consequence (D-M3S04-04), the still-open Q24 layout-default gap (O-M3S04-01), the recurring Billing-queue routing-address risk (O-M3S04-02), and a check_rtm.py skill-depth signal on its dual-key derivation for rule-container types (O-M3S04-03); wrote 5 workbook rows (CWB-AUT-010..012 in Section 6, CWB-OTHER-023..024 in Other Configuration); added 2 traceability rows (REQ-036 the assignment rule, REQ-037 the auto-response rule) and 2 Requirement-id-derivation entries; ran check_rtm.py from the build dir (37 rows, 0 coverage gaps, 0 errors, 2 orphans explained by O-M3S04-03, exit 0); set the step to `documented`.
confidence_rationale: Every artefact produced a workbook row with a real source_req_id and a verification cell, and both new requirements have a traceability row (the HIGH conditions), but two things needed judgment rather than a mechanical read: the check_rtm.py orphan WARN required deciding which of two checker-derived component keys is canonical for the artefact cell (recorded as O-M3S04-03) and the step's own Account-support-tier title/manual-test mismatch remains genuinely open at the M3 gate rather than resolved by this pass.

process_observations.observation: Both checker predictions recorded in the step's own plan.json inputs.note reproduced exactly at run time: check_assignment_rules.py's exit-1 duplicate-target message and check_case_management_setup.py's exit-0 pass, at both build and step scope.

The auto-response rule's senderEmail and replyToEmail both avoid this org's two live Email-to-Case routing addresses, matching the operator's binding pre-gate note and both cited gotchas' mail-loop prohibition.
deploy-order.md is undeclared in M3-S04's outputs[] for a fourth consecutive M3 step, so check-outputs has never adjudicated it.

Q24's assignment-rule-checkbox default remains unwritten after three prior recordings (D-M1S02-03), and owner-writer-map.md now states the concrete consequence: roughly 20 hand-logged cases a day get neither an owner nor an acknowledgement without it.

The step's title and its first manual acceptance test assert Account-support-tier routing that no answered clarification or grounded skill notation lets this build write, carried to the M3 gate as D-M3S04-02 rather than resolved here.

evidence.query: plan.json steps[M3-S04].title vs acceptance_tests[3]; artefacts/M3-S04/deploy-order.md section 6 row 1

process_observations.observation: check_rtm.py reports 2 orphans for this step's own components because its RULE_CONTAINERS derivation registers a second, singular per-rule key alongside the container key the manifest and every other row in this build actually names; 0 coverage gaps and 0 errors otherwise.

milestone-verifier should run once every M3 step is documented, because F-28's org-wide-address prerequisite and the open gate decisions (D-M3S02-04, D-M3S04-02, D-M3S03-02) all need one human adjudication pass across the whole milestone rather than four separate ones.
